sentences.text: Elsornis is classified as a genus of enantiornithean bird.
Only one species, Elsornis keni, has been named within this genus.
The fossil skeleton is extremely well preserved in three dimensions.
It preserves a pneumatized furcula, a feature previously unknown in enantiornitheans.
The genus name combines the Mongolian word for sand and the Greek word for bird.
The species name keni honors Mr. Ken Hayashibara.
The holotype fossil carries the catalogue number MPD-b 100/201.
The fossil was collected at Togrogiin Shiree in the Djadokhta Formation.
Researchers Chiappe et al. (2007) concluded that Elsornis was flightless or nearly so based on its pectoral skeleton proportions.
It is hypothesized that Elsornis may have glided like Archaeopteryx to pounce on ground prey.
Alternatively, Elsornis may have hunted on the ground by snatching small vertebrates and insects.
Elsornis likely possessed small, non-serrated teeth for hunting and possibly scavenged carcasses left by larger carnivores.
A 2018 study by Atterholt et al. places Elsornis in the family Avisauridae.
Elsornis lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
It lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
